key_insight: A mixed finite element formulation couples sediment concentration, temperature, and flow to model heat-assisted consolidation–sedimentation.
engineering_relevance: The model supports simulation of thermally assisted settling of mineral suspensions, where heat, solids transport, and fluid motion interact.
method: Formulate the quasi-stationary coupled system using pseudostress and concentration and temperature gradient variables.
Establish continuous well-posedness using Babuška–Brezzi theory and Banach’s fixed-point theorem.
Develop a mixed finite element discretization with discrete existence and Céa-type a priori error estimates.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples demonstrate model performance and confirm theoretical convergence rates; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Continuous existence and uniqueness require small-data and additional solution-regularity assumptions; this is a numerical PDE method, not an AI surrogate.
paper_title: Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation
